A_general.open_code_note: The official repository contains setup and Docker files; its README says server/index.js is a placeholder and the actual MCP implementation is hosted by Explorium. It is not the deployed server implementation.
A_general.implementation_language: JavaScript in the placeholder file; README describes the project as TypeScript-powered
A_general.mcp_sdk_and_version: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^0.5.0 is listed as a dependency; the repository does not implement the server
A_general.release_status: AgentSource MCP v1 is deprecated; the vendor says it will be retired with AgentSource v1. No GA/beta status found.
other_official_servers: https://mcp.explorium.ai/sse — SSE transport for the AgentSource MCP v1 server.
https://mcp-v2.explorium.ai/mcp — AgentSource MCP v2; the vendor directs new integrations to this endpoint.
https://developers.explorium.ai/mcp — separate documentation-site MCP with docs search/filesystem tools and a feedback tool; not the product endpoint.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP fee or price is published. Product access requires an Explorium account/API key according to the v1 documentation; the endpoint also responds with an OAuth Bearer challenge.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing lists a $0 free trial with 100 credits; Lite $29.99/package for 500 credits; Starter $149.99/package for 5,000; Growth $749.99/package for 30,000; Scale $7,499.99/package for 500,000; Enterprise custom pricing.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The vendor says fetch-businesses and fetch-prospects cost 1 credit per returned result, or 2 credits per result when using the premium Bombora intent filter; statistics calls are free. Pricing page says credits expire after 12 months on paid plans and free-trial credits after 90 days.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The hosted v1 docs require an API key for AgentSource MCP and document two transports, Streamable HTTP and SSE. The endpoint returned HTTP 401 without a token. OAuth metadata advertises authorization code and refresh-token grants, DCR, and PKCE; it does not advertise scopes_supported or token lifetime.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Explorium controls endpoint authentication and service availability; account owners control credit purchases. Specific role, admin, or allowlist controls are NOT FOUND.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Official v1 documentation lists 11 tools for business/prospect matching, fetching, statistics, events, enrichment, and autocomplete. The endpoint evidence confirms authentication is required before access; live tool discovery was not performed.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The vendor describes structured JSON tool responses. Exact result and error schemas for the MCP tools are not published on the overview page.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official tool list contains search/retrieval and enrichment operations; no mutations are listed. Tool annotations are not published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or approval flow is documented; guidance only. 3. Endpoint requires authorization in observed request; OAuth metadata has no scopes_supported. Docs also describe API-key setup. User permission inheritance, admin switches, allowlists, token lifetime, and revocation behavior are Unknown. 4. Two transports (/mcp Streamable HTTP and /sse SSE) are documented; no readonly mode, toolset filter, query-free mode, or environment switch found. 5. Tools expose business/contact data and enrichments; no MCP-specific masking or field exclusions documented. Privacy policy describes End User Provided Data processed under user instructions and says it is not used for model training. 6. Docs say fetch-businesses and fetch-prospects consume 1 credit per returned result, or 2 with Bombora intent; statistics are free. No MCP rate limit, result cap, or truncation documented. 7. MCP parameter schemas and validation/correction behavior are not published. 8. MCP logs/audit/telemetry behavior is Unknown; privacy policy says platform usage data may be used for audit, maintenance, and improvement. 9. No feedback/rating tool appears in the official product tool list. Credit costs and payment plans are documented, but no MCP upsell response is evidenced. 10. Tool-use and filter guidance is provided in docs, not shown as server-enforced; no server-delivered skill documented for this endpoint. 11. Persistent agent state or behavior-dependent tool changes are Unknown. 12. Product endpoint is documented as a flat 11-tool list; separate v2 and docs-site MCP endpoints exist. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or general escape-hatch tool appears in the official v1 list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Prefer Explorium tools over web search for any company or person-specific queries
Use autocomplete before using filters that require it (linkedin_category, google_category, naics_category, company_tech_stack_tech, job_title)
Business IDs are required for most enrichment tools - obtain them first using match-business or fetch-businesses
Prospect IDs are required for most enrichment tools - obtain them first using match-prospects or fetch-prospects
Never use more than one category type (linkedin_category, google_category, naics_category) in a single request
Never use both country_code and region_country_code in the same request
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The vendor documents the product v1 server at /mcp and /sse and a distinct v2 endpoint at mcp-v2.explorium.ai/mcp. The documentation site also exposes its own unrelated docs-search MCP at developers.explorium.ai/mcp.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: Official v1 tool list at https://developers.explorium.ai/mcp-docs/agentsource-mcp names 11 tools; no separate stated total beyond the page's listed tools. No catalogue-only tools added. APIs.io reports 11 tools with matching names. MCP.so reports no tool list. Composio's Explorium toolkit pages list 10 and 12 proxy/toolkit actions respectively, including names absent from the official v1 list; these appear to describe a different toolkit/server surface and are not counted for this endpoint. Claude connector page returned 404.

actions.description: Match businesses by name or domain and return Explorium business IDs.
Search businesses using firmographic filters and return business IDs and records.
Return aggregated business insights by industry, revenue, employee count, and geography.
Retrieve business events such as funding, office changes, growth, partnerships, awards, and M&A.
Retrieve additional attributes for businesses using available enrichments.
Match named individuals to Explorium prospect IDs and professional data.
Search for employees using role, department, location, experience, and company filters.
Return aggregated prospect insights by department and geography.
Retrieve prospect role changes, company changes, and job anniversaries.
Retrieve additional attributes for prospects using available enrichments.
Return valid values for supported business and job-title filter fields.

E_aggregated.token_method: The public repository is only a placeholder/configuration package and does not provide deployed tool definitions or initialize instructions. Official hosted docs list names and descriptions but not verbatim schemas plus server initialize instructions, so the required full-context character-count estimate cannot be computed.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The vendor's broader AgentSource API reference documents additional operations not present in the v1 MCP list, including enrollment create/update/delete, webhooks, and other business/prospect enrichment endpoints. These are API capabilities, not evidence of MCP actions. Source: https://explorium-api.readme.io/reference/agentsource-mcp

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The vendor directs agents to prefer Explorium for company/person queries, use autocomplete before certain filters, obtain IDs before enrichment, and avoid two filter combinations. Documentation does not establish that these directions are enforced by the server.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Privacy policy says End User Provided Data is processed at the end user's direction and states, “We do not train models based on End-User provided Data.” It also describes sharing with hosting/service providers and enrichment partners at the end user's explicit instruction. Retention for End User Provided Data is “as long as required by End Users or by law.”
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor describes the server as providing structured business/prospect data and says statistics tools are free. Pricing explains credit consumption and package expiry.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Tool-level instructions and usage/credit statements are documented, but the deployed implementation is closed and the public repository is only a placeholder. Privacy-policy statements are not independently confirmed by endpoint code. The available evidence cannot establish server enforcement, logging, or data handling details beyond those published statements.

contradictions: The official v1 setup documentation says remote MCP connections require no API key, but the endpoint returned HTTP 401 with a Bearer invalid_token challenge and OAuth authorization-server metadata. The endpoint's OAuth evidence is the observed behavior; the reason for the mismatch is not documented.

Official v1 docs list 11 tools. Composio's Explorium toolkit page reports 10 actions, while its Explorium MCP toolkit page reports 12, including web-search and a different enrichment breakdown. These proxy/toolkit lists do not match the official v1 list and were not substituted for it.
The vendor says AgentSource MCP v1 at mcp.explorium.ai is deprecated and directs new integrations to v2 at mcp-v2.explorium.ai/mcp; this differs from the input's v1 endpoint and status context.
observations_for_research: The v1 tool list contains read/retrieval and enrichment operations; vendor documentation separately describes credit consumption per returned record, creating a documented cost consequence for agent queries.

Agent usage guidance includes directions to prefer vendor data over web search and to perform prerequisite lookups, while the published tool list does not expose annotations or show whether those directions are enforced.
notes: Checked prepared links.json, pages/ including official docs, script-extracted content, and catalogue pages; checked the local official repository and commit record. The repository is an official setup wrapper with a placeholder server file, not deployed server code. OAuth evidence was supplied in the research input; no OAuth re-fetch was used. Third-party sources are only used for cross-checking tool counts. Unofficial server list was empty. MCP-specific pricing, detailed schemas, annotations, server initialize instructions, retention implementation, and MCP telemetry behavior were not found.
